name: Pioneer 10

hotspots.label: Look out into deep interstellar space

parts.name: Big parabolic dish
parts.role: 2.74-meter high-gain parabolic antenna beaming weak signals across billions of kilometers
parts.snap: High-gain dish mounted to face Earth.

parts.name: Central instrument hub
parts.role: Hexagonal equipment compartment housing scientific electronics and transmitters

parts.name: Two RTG booms
parts.role: Snap-19 nuclear thermoelectric generators mounted on deployable trusses
parts.snap: RTG booms deployed to isolate radiation from sensors.

parts.name: Magnetometer boom
parts.role: Extended 5.8-meter boom holding helium vector magnetometer sensors

parts.name: Photopolarimeter
parts.role: Imaging photopolarimeter that took the first close-up pictures of Jupiter
parts.snap: Photopolarimeter calibrated for gas giant imagery.

parts.name: Gold pictorial plaque
parts.role: Gold-anodized aluminum plaque showing human figures and Earth's celestial coordinates
parts.snap: Pioneer plaque attached for interstellar wanderers.

challenge.title: Keep the signal alive
challenge.intro: Electrical output from the RTG decays over decades. Power down non-essential instruments as the years advance, keeping the transmitter online until the final signal.
challenge.hint: The transmitter must stay powered. Toggle instruments off until power usage fits within the year's available wattage.

signal_note: A final whisper was received on January 23, 2003 from 12 billion kilometers away, after which power fell below transmission levels.
ending: Pioneer 10 is drifting toward the constellation Taurus, carrying humanity's message into interstellar space.
